wine_name: Shafer Vineyards One Point Five, Napa Valley
wrong_facts: Hook says 'sources from younger estate vines in Stags Leap District' — ground truth shows it's multi-site (Shafer hillside estate, Borderline vineyard in Stags Leap District, AND selected Napa Valley sites), not just younger estate vines in Stags Leap
Hook says '100% Cab' — ground truth 2022 blend is 92% Cabernet Sauvignon, 3% Petite Verdot, 3% Merlot, 2% Malbec
Vinification says '20 months in French oak' — ground truth is 18 months in 100% new French oak
Vinification says 'mostly new' oak — ground truth is 100% new French oak
Wine summary references '1976 Judgment of Paris where a Shafer relative shone' — Shafer had no involvement in the 1976 Judgment of Paris; this is fabricated
Wine summary claims '50 hillside acres' — not in context data and unverifiable
Spottswoode is NOT in Stags Leap District — it's in St. Helena
No mention of the actual naming origin (generation and a half between John and Doug Shafer)
reasoning: The hook contains two provably wrong claims: calling it 100% Cab (it's a 92% Cab blend) and mischaracterizing the sourcing as 'younger estate vines in Stags Leap District' when it's multi-site. The Judgment of Paris reference involving Shafer is fabricated — Stag's Leap Wine Cellars (a different producer) was in the Judgment, not Shafer Vineyards. Oak aging is stated as 20 months mostly new when ground truth is 18 months 100% new. Multiple fabricated numbers (20 months, 50 acres, 122,735 acres) trigger the hard cap. The voice is decent — direct and opinionated without banned words — but the factual errors are severe and undermine the entire output.
